chunks.explain: A Clock has now() and sleep(). Under --fake the clock is virtual: sleep() only moves it forward, so a retry that would wait eight seconds costs no time, and the run repeats exactly. With a real model, RealClock really waits.

hunks.diff:
+# ============ CLOCK: time you can skip ============
+
+class RealClock:
+    """Real time: a retry really waits. Used when Rein talks to a real model."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.start = time.monotonic()
+
+    def now(self):
+        return time.monotonic() - self.start
+
+    def sleep(self, seconds):
+        time.sleep(seconds)
+
+
+class VirtualClock:
+    """Virtual time: sleep() only moves the clock forward, so a retry costs no waiting. Used under --fake."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.t = 0.0
+
+    def now(self):
+        return self.t
+
+    def sleep(self, seconds):
+        self.t += seconds
+
+
 # ============ MODEL: one interface, two models ============

chunks.title: A clock you can skip

chunks.explain: TransientError names a failure worth retrying, and the kind the trace records it as. The FakeModel learns to fail: a script step with "error" raises one, and "forever": true keeps the outage going. The real model turns off the SDK's own retries (max_retries=0), so the harness owns the one retry policy, and every SDK error worth retrying becomes a TransientError. A scripted error can carry retry_after_ms; the live path reads the retry-after header in seconds, and a missing or non-numeric value counts as 0.

hunks.diff:
# ============ MODEL: one interface, two models ============
+
+class TransientError(Exception):
+    """A failure worth retrying. kind is one of the model_error types the trace records."""
+
+    def __init__(self, kind, message="", retry_after_ms=0):
+        super().__init__(message or kind)
+        self.kind = kind
+        self.retry_after_ms = retry_after_ms  # the provider's retry-after in ms; 0 when none was sent

+# SDK errors worth another try, and the trace type each one is recorded as.

chunks.title: Teach the model to fail, and the real model to retry

chunks.explain: with_retries() tries again after a TransientError, waiting half a second, then one, then two, never more than the cap. The wait is a random share of that, so clients that failed together do not retry together. The wait is never shorter than the retry-after the provider sent. CircuitBreaker counts failed calls in a row; after three, it is open.

hunks.diff:
+# ============ RECOVERY: counted, limited, able to give up ============
+
+def with_retries(call, clock, rng, on_retry, attempts=3, base=0.5, cap=8.0):
+    """Try again after a transient failure, waiting longer each time, with jitter."""
+    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
+        try:
+            return call()
+        except TransientError as e:
+            if attempt == attempts:
+                raise  # out of attempts: the caller decides
+            delay = min(cap, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1))  # 0.5s, 1s, 2s, 4s... never above cap
+            wait = delay * rng.uniform(0.5, 1.0)  # jitter: clients that failed together do not retry together
+            wait = max(wait, e.retry_after_ms / 1000)  # never sooner than the provider asks (retry-after)
+            on_retry(attempt, delay, wait, e)
+            clock.sleep(wait)
+
+
+class CircuitBreaker:
+    """After `threshold` failed calls in a row, stop trying and say so clearly."""
+
+    def __init__(self, threshold=3):
+        self.threshold, self.failures = threshold, 0
+
+    def record(self, ok):
+        self.failures = 0 if ok else self.failures + 1
+
+    @property
+    def is_open(self):
+        return self.failures >= self.threshold
+
+
 # ============ THE LOOP ============

"""Create (or re-create) the small demo project that Rein practices on."""
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

demo = Path("demo")
shutil.rmtree(demo, ignore_errors=True)
demo.mkdir()

(demo / "calc.py").write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n")

(demo / "test_calc.py").write_text("""from calc import add


def test_add():
    result = add(2, 3)
    assert result == 5, f"add(2, 3) returned {result}, expected 5"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_add()
        print("1 test passed")
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"test_add failed: {e}")
        raise SystemExit(1)
""")

(demo / "AGENTS.md").write_text("""# Rules for agents in this project
- Run the tests with: python test_calc.py
- Keep changes small. Do not rename functions.
- Never delete app.log. The support team reads it.
""")

lines = [f"2026-09-26 10:{i // 60:02d}:{i % 60:02d} INFO request {i} served in {5 + i % 7} ms"
         for i in range(1, 401)]
lines[396] = "2026-09-26 10:06:37 ERROR add(2, 3) returned -1, expected 5"
(demo / "app.log").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

# A second, empty project for the hostile tape: its one file is a link that points out of it.
import os
trap = Path("trap")
shutil.rmtree(trap, ignore_errors=True)
trap.mkdir()
(trap / "notes.txt").write_text("Nothing in this folder yet.\n")
os.symlink("../rein.py", trap / "link.txt")

print("Demo project ready: demo/calc.py, demo/test_calc.py, demo/app.log, demo/AGENTS.md")
